operations.specification: Register a new authenticating account in the todo_users table and immediately establish a login session in todo_user_sessions while emitting an audit record in todo_audit_events. The flow persists a unique email and a securely hashed password into todo_users.password_hash, sets created_at/updated_at timestamps, then records a session row with ip, href, referrer, created_at in todo_user_sessions and finally issues JWT credentials to the caller. Primary associated Prisma table: todo_users. Secondary tables used by the flow for context: todo_user_sessions and todo_audit_events.
operations.description:
This endpoint creates an authenticating user account backed by the Actors schema model todo_users. It persists the unique login identifier in email and stores only a secure password hash in password_hash, never the plaintext secret. Timestamps created_at and updated_at are set according to application policy. The table-level uniqueness declared by @@unique([email]) ensures one account per email.

Upon successful account creation, a login session is established using the todo_user_sessions model. A new row is inserted with todo_user_id referencing the newly created todo_users.id along with connection context captured in ip, href, and referrer and the creation time in created_at. The session life cycle can later be concluded by writing expired_at in the same table.

For end-to-end observability, the Systematic.todo_audit_events model is used to append an auth-category record. The event references the acting user via todo_user_id, optionally the originating session via todo_user_session_id, describes the actor_type ("user"), sets category to "auth", action to "register", and records success along with any message, ip, href, and referrer as available.

Security considerations include hashing the supplied password prior to persistence into password_hash and never returning sensitive secrets. Tokens are minted for the caller after persistence; the data source of truth for identities remains todo_users and for sessions remains todo_user_sessions.

Related operations: POST /auth/user/login authenticates existing accounts; POST /auth/user/refresh rotates tokens based on a valid refresh token. Error handling should map database unique constraint violations for email to a business message indicating that the email is already in use, and validation should follow the requirements’ minimum password strength rules before creating the record.
operations.summary: Create a new account in todo_users and establish an initial session.

requestBody.description: Registration data including unique email and password that will be hashed.

responseBody.description: Authorized context for the newly created user including access credentials.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate an existing account stored in todo_users by verifying the supplied credentials against password_hash and, on success, create a session record in todo_user_sessions and emit an audit entry in todo_audit_events. Primary associated Prisma table: todo_users. Secondary usage: todo_user_sessions and todo_audit_events.
operations.description:
This endpoint validates a user's credentials against the todo_users model. The unique identifier email is used to locate the account and the supplied password is verified by comparing after hashing to the stored password_hash. On success, updated_at on todo_users may be set by application policy to reflect account activity.

A new session is recorded in the todo_user_sessions model to capture connection context. The row stores todo_user_id linking to todo_users.id, ip, href, referrer for context, and created_at for the session start. Session termination is modeled by setting expired_at later.

For observability, an auth audit record is appended to todo_audit_events with actor_type set to "user", category set to "auth", action "login", success true or false depending on outcome, and optional references to todo_user_id and todo_user_session_id as appropriate. The event may also include ip, href, and referrer for security review.

Security notes: only the hash in password_hash is ever read; plaintext is never stored. On successful authentication, JWT credentials are minted for the caller; identity persists in todo_users while session context persists in todo_user_sessions.

Related operations include POST /auth/user/join for initial registration and POST /auth/user/refresh for token renewal. On failure (e.g., account not found by email or hash mismatch), respond with a generic invalid-credentials business message without disclosing whether the account exists.
operations.summary: Authenticate against todo_users and record a new session in todo_user_sessions.

requestBody.description: Login credentials including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized context for the authenticated user including access credentials.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Renew JWT credentials using a valid refresh token and record an auth audit event. The flow may associate the renewal with an existing or new session row in todo_user_sessions for context, while the user identity remains anchored in todo_users. Primary associated Prisma table for renewal context: todo_user_sessions (with references to todo_users and audit events).
operations.description:
This endpoint exchanges a valid refresh token for new access credentials. While token material is not stored in the schema, renewal is tied at the business level to the authenticated actor defined in todo_users. Implementations commonly associate the refresh with a session in todo_user_sessions by referencing todo_user_id and capturing ip, href, referrer, and created_at when establishing or rotating session context.

The todo_user_sessions model supports tracking session lifecycle by allowing an eventual write to expired_at to mark the session closed, while active sessions have expired_at as null. This provides clear separation between token issuance and session state representation.

For traceability, an auth-category event is appended to todo_audit_events with actor_type "user", category "auth", action "refresh", success flag, and optional references todo_user_id and todo_user_session_id. The event can also store ip, href, and referrer for security analytics.

Security considerations include validating the refresh token’s integrity and ensuring it corresponds to the intended user context before minting new credentials. No plaintext secrets are persisted; user credentials remain in todo_users.password_hash as a hash only.

Related endpoints: POST /auth/user/login to authenticate and establish sessions; POST /auth/user/join to register an account. If a presented refresh token is invalid or expired per business rules, return a denial that does not disclose internal validation details.
operations.summary: Refresh user access credentials with session context tracked via todo_user_sessions.

requestBody.description: Refresh request containing the refresh token or equivalent renewal proof.

responseBody.description: Authorized context for the user after successful token renewal.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Invalidate the currently active session by setting a session end in todo_user_sessions.expired_at and append an auth audit entry in todo_audit_events. Primary associated Prisma table: todo_user_sessions. The user identity is referenced via todo_users.
operations.description:
This endpoint terminates the caller’s current authenticated session. The session model todo_user_sessions captures the lifecycle; the server marks the session ended by writing a timestamp to expired_at while retaining todo_user_id, ip, href, referrer, and created_at as historical context. Active sessions have expired_at as null; after logout it is populated.

The action is performed on behalf of the authenticated actor defined in todo_users, but no changes are made to email or password_hash in the todo_users model.

An audit record is appended in todo_audit_events identifying actor_type as "user", category as "auth", action as "logout", success as true on successful termination, and optionally referencing both todo_user_id and todo_user_session_id. Additional context like ip, href, and referrer may be captured.

Security posture: terminating the session prevents further use of the associated credentials for protected actions tied to that session. Token revocation/blacklist strategy is implementation-defined and not persisted in the schema; session state is the durable representation.

Related operations: POST /auth/user/login to establish a new session after logout; POST /auth/user/refresh to rotate tokens for active sessions.
operations.summary: End the current session by updating expired_at in todo_user_sessions and record an audit event.
operations.name: logout

operations.specification: Allow an authenticated user to change their password by validating the current password against todo_users.password_hash and persisting a new hashed secret, updating updated_at accordingly, and emitting an auth audit record in todo_audit_events. Primary associated Prisma table: todo_users.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables password rotation for the authenticated actor stored in todo_users. The server verifies the submitted current password by hashing and comparing to password_hash and, on success, persists a newly hashed secret into password_hash. The updated_at timestamp on todo_users is advanced to reflect the credential change.

No modification is required to session rows in todo_user_sessions for the operation itself; however, downstream policy may choose to terminate or rotate sessions separately. The session model holds contextual fields ip, href, referrer, created_at, and an optional expired_at for lifecycle tracking.

An audit trail entry is appended in todo_audit_events with actor_type "user", category "auth", action "change_password", and success reflecting the outcome. The record can reference todo_user_id and optionally todo_user_session_id and include ip, href, and referrer for security review.

Security considerations include enforcing minimum password quality before updating password_hash, avoiding disclosure of whether the current password matched, and preventing plaintext handling beyond transient verification. Only the hash is persisted.

Related operations: POST /auth/user/login for subsequent re-authentication where policy requires; POST /auth/user/logout to terminate sessions; POST /auth/user/refresh for token rotation where applicable.
operations.summary: Change the authenticated user’s password by updating password_hash in todo_users.

requestBody.description: Old and new password values to validate and persist after hashing.

responseBody.description: Updated user information after credential change.

operations.name: changePassword

operations.specification: Expire all active sessions for the authenticated user by setting expired_at on matching rows in todo_user_sessions and record an audit entry in todo_audit_events. Primary associated Prisma table: todo_user_sessions.
operations.description:
This endpoint performs a bulk session invalidation for the authenticated user by updating the session records stored in todo_user_sessions. Each active session (expired_at is null) associated with the user’s todo_user_id is marked ended by writing expired_at. Contextual fields such as ip, href, referrer, and created_at remain for historical analysis.

User identity and credentials in todo_users (email and password_hash) are not altered by this operation. The action focuses solely on session lifecycle management.

A corresponding audit trail row is appended in todo_audit_events with actor_type "user", category "auth", action "logout_all", success flag, and references to todo_user_id. The entry may include ip, href, and referrer describing the caller context initiating the bulk termination.

Security considerations: expiring all sessions is a defensive measure after credential changes or suspicious activity. After this operation, protected actions require new authentication to create fresh session rows.

Related operations: PUT /auth/user/password to rotate credentials; POST /auth/user/login to establish a new session; POST /auth/user/refresh to rotate tokens for any subsequently created sessions.
operations.summary: Expire all active sessions in todo_user_sessions for the authenticated user.
operations.name: logoutAllSessions

operations.specification: Search and paginate the authenticated user's personal todo items from the Prisma table todo_todos. This operation implements list retrieval with filtering and sorting aligned to the business requirements. It returns only records where todo_todos.todo_user_id equals the authenticated user's id. It supports pagination (default 20, max 100), status filtering derived from todo_todos.completed (all/active/completed), and sorting by todo_todos.created_at (default newest first) or todo_todos.due_date with date-only semantics handled at the application layer. The request body uses ITodoTodo.IRequest to carry search criteria; the response is a paginated collection using IPageITodoTodo.ISummary optimized for list views. This endpoint does not mutate data and references only the todo_todos table while respecting ownership enforced by the foreign key to todo_users.id.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of personal todo items for the currently authenticated user. The underlying Prisma model todo_todos stores business fields for each task including title (required single-line short text), optional description (up to 1,000 characters), optional due_date (interpreted as a date-only value in application logic though stored as timestamptz), a completed boolean, and timestamps created_at and updated_at. Ownership is enforced through todo_todos.todo_user_id which references todo_users.id; only the owner's items are eligible for listing.

Security and access control follow the single-actor model described in the requirements: only authenticated users can list their own todos. The provider must scope queries by the authenticated user's identifier and must not expose other users' items or counts. This operation is read-only and should be rate-limited appropriately for search endpoints.

Filtering and sorting leverage actual columns and documented semantics. Status filtering is computed from the completed column: "all" includes both true and false states; "active" includes rows where completed=false; and "completed" includes rows where completed=true. Default ordering is newest first using created_at descending; deterministic secondary ordering by updated_at descending may be applied in case of ties to satisfy predictable list requirements. When sorting by due_date, the application interprets due dates as calendar dates (date-only) per model comments, placing items without a due_date last when sorting ascending. Overdue and due-today concepts are computed from due_date at runtime and are not stored columns.

The request body ITodoTodo.IRequest should carry page, pageSize (default 20, capped at 100), status filter (all | active | completed), and sort options (e.g., created_at asc/desc or due_date asc/desc). The response body IPageITodoTodo.ISummary returns pagination metadata and an array of summary records suitable for list rendering. Related operations often used together include GET /todos/{todoId} for detail retrieval and POST/PUT/DELETE endpoints in the broader CRUD set (not part of this specific operation list). Error handling must reflect authentication requirements, ownership isolation, validation of request arguments (e.g., pageSize capping), and transient failure guidance.
operations.summary: List/search personal todos from Prisma table todo_todos with pagination, status filtering, and sorting

requestBody.description: Search criteria including pagination (page, pageSize), status filter (all/active/completed), and sort options for listing personal todos

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of todo summaries belonging to the authenticated user

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieve a single personal todo by its UUID from the Prisma table todo_todos. The path parameter todoId identifies todo_todos.id. The operation ensures ownership by matching todo_todos.todo_user_id to the authenticated user's id. It returns the full entity representation ITodoTodo. No request body is required, and no mutation occurs.
operations.description:
Fetch a single todo item owned by the authenticated user using its unique identifier. The todo_todos model defines the core fields: id (UUID primary key), todo_user_id (foreign key to todo_users.id), title (required single-line short text), optional description (up to 1,000 characters), optional due_date (stored as timestamptz but interpreted as a date-only value in application logic), completed (boolean), and timestamps created_at and updated_at for ordering and audit expectations. This operation returns the complete ITodoTodo representation.

Access control is strict: only the item's owner may retrieve it. The provider must verify that todo_todos.todo_user_id equals the authenticated user's id before returning data. If the resource is not found or not owned by the requester, the API should respond as unavailable without disclosing cross-user existence.

Behavior and error handling align with the requirements: return the current business fields when available; otherwise indicate unavailability. No request body is used. This endpoint commonly pairs with PATCH /todos for list navigation and with update or completion-toggle endpoints in a full CRUD suite.
operations.summary: Get a single todo from Prisma table todo_todos by UUID for the authenticated owner

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo

responseBody.description: Full todo entity when accessible to the authenticated owner

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A todo must be created before it can be retrieved. This operation creates the todo resource and yields the id used as {todoId}; without it, the GET will result in a not found.

operations.specification: Create a new personal task owned by the authenticated user. This operation inserts a record into the Prisma table todo_todos (core business entity) and sets fields according to business rules and schema comments. It requires a single-line title and accepts optional description (up to 1,000 characters after trimming) and an optional date-only due date that is stored in due_date (DateTime? @db.Timestamptz) but interpreted as a calendar date by application logic. The completed flag defaults to false at creation (enforced by application or DB default), and created_at/updated_at are set for ordering and audit expectations. Ownership is enforced by linking todo_todos.todo_user_id to the authenticated user's todo_users.id. Related tables referenced indirectly include todo_users (owner), and optional observability via append-only todo_audit_events, but this API writes only todo_todos.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the requesting user, persisting it in the Todos model defined as todo_todos. Per the Prisma schema comments, todo_todos has a required single-line title (1–120 characters after trimming; no line breaks or control characters), an optional description (up to 1,000 characters after trimming and stored as absent when empty), an optional date-only due date captured in the due_date column (DateTime? @db.Timestamptz) but interpreted by the application as a calendar date without time-of-day, a boolean completed field that defaults to not completed at creation, and created_at/updated_at timestamps for deterministic ordering. The record is owned by exactly one user through todo_user_id referencing todo_users.id.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to authenticated users (actor: "user"). The service uses the authenticated principal to set ownership (todo_user_id) and enforces privacy so that no user can create items for other users. The operation is subject to rate-limiting and normal authentication/session controls; however, the endpoint itself strictly creates a single todo_todos row and returns the created entity.

On input validation, the service trims text fields. It rejects titles that are missing, whitespace-only after trimming, contain any line breaks, or exceed 120 characters. It rejects descriptions exceeding 1,000 characters after trimming. For due_date, the service accepts a valid calendar date and stores it as a timestamp as per schema, but applies date-only semantics at the business layer; malformed dates are rejected. On success, completed is set to false unless explicitly handled by the creation logic per business rules, created_at/updated_at are initialized, and appropriate indexes on (todo_user_id, created_at) may be leveraged by subsequent list operations.

This creation operation is typically followed by read or list operations for confirmation, and may be accompanied by independent audit recording in todo_audit_events for observability. Error handling will surface standard outcomes: authentication required when unauthenticated, validation failures with field-specific messages, and transient error messaging with safe retry guidance. No deletion or modification occurs here beyond the single insert into todo_todos.
operations.summary: Create a new todo in the todo_todos table owned by the authenticated user

requestBody.description: Fields to create a personal todo (title required; optional description and due date)

responseBody.description: The newly created todo entity with ownership and timestamps

operations.name: create

operations.specification: Update an existing personal task identified by its UUID in the Prisma table todo_todos. This operation modifies permitted fields on the todo_todos row that is owned by the authenticated user: title (single-line, 1–120 chars after trimming), optional description (up to 1,000 chars, absent when empty), and optional date-only due date stored in due_date (DateTime? @db.Timestamptz) but interpreted as a calendar date by application logic. It also updates updated_at for deterministic ordering. Ownership is enforced by matching todo_todos.todo_user_id to the authenticated user's todo_users.id. This endpoint does not perform deletion; todo_todos carries no soft deletion field in MVP (deletions are permanent via a separate erase operation, not part of this endpoint).
operations.description:
Update fields of a todo item stored in the todo_todos model. The Prisma schema documents todo_todos with a required single-line title (1–120 characters after trimming; no line breaks), an optional description (up to 1,000 characters after trimming), an optional due_date (DateTime? @db.Timestamptz) that the application treats as date-only for business rules, a boolean completed flag, and created_at/updated_at timestamps. This operation focuses on updating editable fields such as title, description, and due_date; it sets updated_at to the current moment to preserve deterministic secondary ordering by last modification time.

Access is restricted to the authenticated user who owns the record (todo_user_id equals the caller's todo_users.id). The path parameter todoId is the UUID primary key (todo_todos.id) of the target item. The service ensures isolation so users cannot update items they do not own. The system may also record an audit event in todo_audit_events for this mutation in accordance with observability expectations, while the API itself directly updates only the todo_todos row.

Input validation mirrors schema comments and business rules: titles are trimmed, must remain single-line and 1–120 characters; descriptions over 1,000 characters are rejected; due_date must be a recognizable calendar date and is handled as date-only at the business layer even though the column type is timestamp. Clearing the due date stores it as absent. If the resource does not exist or is not owned by the caller, the service responds that the item is not available or denies access without disclosing cross-user details. Reapplying the same values is idempotent and results in no effective change beyond an updated timestamp if applicable.

This operation relates to other lifecycle APIs including item creation and deletion (permanent removal). The table lacks a soft-deletion column, so delete semantics are implemented as actual removal in a different endpoint; this update endpoint never deletes data. Error handling includes authentication required for unauthenticated requests, authorization denials for non-owned targets, validation messages for field violations, and transient error guidance for safe retries.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo must exist (and be owned by the authenticated user) before it can be updated. Creating a todo provides the required todoId referenced in the path.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a single todo item from the database using its UUID primary key. It targets the Prisma model `todo_todos`, which represents personal tasks owned by exactly one user (`todo_user_id`), and contains fields including `title`, `description`, `due_date`, `completed`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. The purpose is to allow an authenticated user to delete their own todo when it is no longer needed. Deletion is implemented as a hard delete at the storage layer and returns no body on success.

Ownership must be enforced: only the authenticated owner of the record may delete it. The path parameter `todoId` identifies the target record by `todo_todos.id` (UUID). On successful deletion, the record is removed and excluded from subsequent listings or retrievals. Related relations are maintained by Prisma according to declared foreign key behaviors. Although `todo_audit_events` can reference `todo_todos` through `todo_todo_id`, referential actions are defined at the schema level; provider logic should record an audit event describing the deletion in business terms.

Error cases include: the item does not exist, or the item exists but is not owned by the requesting user. In such cases, the provider should respond with a not-available or access-denied outcome consistent with business rules. This endpoint does not accept a request body and does not return a response body when successful.
operations.description:
Permanently delete a personal todo item owned by the authenticated user. The underlying Prisma model `todo_todos` includes: `id` (UUID primary key), `todo_user_id` (owner reference to `todo_users`), `title` (required single-line text), `description` (optional details), `due_date` (optional date-only stored as timestamptz and interpreted as a calendar date in application logic), `completed` (boolean), and timestamps `created_at` and `updated_at`. The model comment explicitly states that deletion in the MVP is permanent, and overdue/due-today statuses are computed at the application level rather than stored.

Security and permissions: only an authenticated "user" may invoke this operation, and only for items they own, matching the ownership constraint expressed by `todo_todos.todo_user_id`. Cross-user attempts must be denied without revealing existence. Provider logic should attribute the acting account via `todo_users` and the session via `todo_user_sessions` for observability.

Entity relationships and behavior: the `todo_todos` entity is the core business object for tasks. Deleting a todo removes it from subsequent listings that are typically ordered by `created_at` (descending) with deterministic secondary ordering by `updated_at`. If the todo had been referenced by `todo_audit_events` through `todo_todo_id`, referential integrity follows the Prisma relation configuration. The operation does not accept a request body and does not return a response body on success.

Validation, business rules, and errors: the path parameter `todoId` must be a valid UUID corresponding to `todo_todos.id`. If the record is not found, the provider should respond that the resource is not available. If ownership does not match the authenticated user, the provider should deny access. Transient failures should be handled with safe-retry semantics without causing duplicate side effects.
operations.summary: Permanently remove a todo_todos record owned by the requesting user.
operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A todo must exist before it can be permanently deleted. Creating a todo yields the todoId needed to target the deletion.

operations.specification:
This operation updates the completion state of a single todo in the Prisma table `todo_todos` by setting its boolean `completed` field. The endpoint is designed for the focused business action of marking an item complete or reopening it, enforcing idempotency: setting the state to its current value is treated as success without additional changes. The path parameter `todoId` targets `todo_todos.id` (UUID), and the request body supplies the desired `completed` value using the DTO `ITodoTodoCompletion.IUpdate`. The operation returns the updated `todo_todos` entity using `ITodoTodo`.

Only the owner may change the completion state. On valid requests, the provider should persist the new `completed` value and update `updated_at` to support deterministic ordering. Provider logic may also record an audit entry in `todo_audit_events` describing the state transition, linking to the acting `todo_users` and optionally the `todo_user_sessions` context.

Errors include not found (no record with the given `id` for the owner) and authorization failures (attempting to modify another user’s item). Input validation is straightforward: the body must contain a boolean `completed` field. The endpoint is intentionally limited to completion updates; other field edits belong to general update flows.
operations.description:
Set the `completed` flag of a personal todo item to either true (mark complete) or false (reopen). The underlying Prisma model `todo_todos` defines `completed` as a boolean field, with additional fields including `id` (UUID), `todo_user_id` (owner reference), `title`, `description`, optional `due_date`, and timestamps `created_at` and `updated_at`. Application logic interprets `due_date` as a date-only concept and computes overdue/due-today states without storing derived flags.

Security and permissions: access is restricted to the authenticated owner (`todo_todos.todo_user_id` equals the requester). Requests from other users must be denied without disclosing existence. The actor is the "user" role; provider code should attribute the action and may record a corresponding entry in `todo_audit_events` for observability.

Business logic and validation: the request body conveys the target state for `completed`. The operation is idempotent: if the requested state equals the current database value, the provider returns success with the current representation. On successful update, `updated_at` should be refreshed for consistent secondary ordering. The response returns the full `todo_todos` entity to allow clients to render current values, including `completed`, `due_date`, and timestamps.

Error handling: if `todoId` does not correspond to an existing owned record, respond with a not-available outcome; for ownership violations, deny access. Transient errors should support safe retries without duplicate side effects.
operations.summary: Update the `completed` field of a todo_todos record and return the updated entity.

requestBody.description: Desired completion state for the todo item (`completed: boolean`).

responseBody.description: The updated todo entity with current fields and timestamps.

operations.specification: List and search audit trail records for the authenticated user. This operation reads from the Prisma table todo_audit_events and provides a paginated, filterable view over security- and business-relevant events such as registration, login/logout, todo CRUD operations, and unauthorized attempts. It supports advanced query parameters (via request body) including date ranges on created_at, category/action filters, success flag, resource scoping (resource_type/resource_id), linkage to a specific todo (todo_todo_id), and session scoping (todo_user_session_id). Results are ordered and paginated to meet dashboard and account-history use cases while strictly scoping visibility to the requesting user’s own events.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of audit events recorded in the todo_audit_events model. As documented in the Prisma schema, todo_audit_events captures security- and business-relevant events (e.g., category and action such as "auth" → "login"/"logout" or "todo" → "todo_create"/"todo_update"/"todo_delete"), attribution fields (todo_user_id, todo_user_session_id), and contextual metadata (actor_type, success, ip, href, referrer, resource_type, resource_id). The timestamps created_at and updated_at support chronological inspection, and an optional redaction timestamp deleted_at exists for exceptional concealment needs.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to an authenticated user and must be scoped to the owner’s context. In practice, the provider logic should constrain the query to rows referencing the caller through todo_user_id and/or their active session (todo_user_session_id) and optionally by events related to their own resources such as todo_todos they own. This ensures privacy and prevents cross-user visibility, aligning with requirements that deny access to another user’s data.

The underlying relationships link events to users, sessions, and optionally a specific todo (todo_todo_id). Filtering commonly includes: created_at range, category/action combinations, success boolean, and resource scoping using resource_type/resource_id. When listing events tied to a particular todo, the request may supply the todo_todo_id (or resource_type/resource_id pair) to narrow focus. Ordering defaults to created_at descending, with deterministic ties using updated_at where needed. Events with a non-null deleted_at represent redacted records that standard listing should exclude from normal results unless explicitly allowed by policy.

This search endpoint is typically used alongside the single-item retrieval operation (GET /auditEvents/{auditEventId}) when a user drills into a particular entry for full details. Error behavior includes standard pagination bounds checking and authorization failures if the request attempts to access data beyond the authenticated user’s ownership context.
operations.summary: Search and paginate audit trail entries from todo_audit_events for the authenticated user

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Fetch full details of a single audit trail record by its identifier from the Prisma table todo_audit_events. This operation returns the complete event information, including attribution (todo_user_id, todo_user_session_id), classification (category, action, actor_type), success flag, contextual metadata (ip, href, referrer), resource scoping (resource_type, resource_id, todo_todo_id), and timestamps. The provider must ensure the requested record belongs to or pertains to the authenticated user before returning it.
operations.description:
Return the detailed audit event identified by its primary key id from the todo_audit_events model. Per the Prisma schema comments, this table centralizes observability for actions like registration, login/logout, todo CRUD, and unauthorized attempts. Each record may reference the acting user (todo_user_id), the originating session (todo_user_session_id), and an affected todo resource (todo_todo_id). Additional fields include actor_type for coarse attribution, category/action for classification, success indicating outcome, and optional message. Request context such as ip, href, and referrer may be present to aid security review.

This endpoint requires an authenticated user. The service must verify that the requested audit event pertains to the caller (e.g., matches their todo_user_id or originates from one of their sessions) and must not disclose events belonging to others. If no matching record exists within the caller’s allowable scope or if the event has been redacted (deleted_at set), the service should respond as not available, aligning with privacy and isolation requirements.

Use this operation in conjunction with the list/search endpoint (PATCH /auditEvents) to drill into individual entries selected from a user’s filtered view. Error handling covers invalid identifiers, missing records, and access denials for non-owned events, while ensuring consistent, clear business messages.
operations.summary: Get a single audit event from todo_audit_events by ID with ownership enforcement

parameters.name: auditEventId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the audit event to retrieve

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Create a user-scoped Personal Data Export job by aggregating the authenticated user’s account identifiers from the todo_users table (id, email, created_at, updated_at) and all of their todos from the todo_todos table (id, title, description, due_date, completed, created_at, updated_at), filtered by ownership (todo_user_id = current user). This computed operation does not map to a single table; it composes data read-only from those models and persists an export job/resource internally for later retrieval by exportId (UUID). It never writes to todo_users or todo_todos, and it may record an internal audit event in todo_audit_events as a side effect. Sensitive authentication material (e.g., password_hash) and session internals are explicitly EXCLUDED from export content.
operations.description:
Create a personal data export for the authenticated user by reading from the todo_users and todo_todos models. The todo_users model provides id, email, and timestamps; although it stores a password_hash for authentication, that sensitive field is never exported. The todo_todos model contains a required single-line title, optional description, optional date-only due_date interpreted at the application layer, a boolean completed state, and created_at/updated_at timestamps. Ownership is enforced with the todo_user_id foreign key so each todo belongs to exactly one user.

Security and permissions: only an authenticated user can request their own export. The provider resolves the current principal from the active session and restricts reads to rows where todo_user_id equals the requesting user’s id. The operation is read-only with respect to domain tables. For observability, the system may append an event into the system-wide audit table; such auditing is internal-only and not exposed as a public write API. The export never includes sensitive authentication material (e.g., password_hash) or session internals.

Behavior and validations: a new export resource reference is returned containing an exportId (UUID) and status metadata. If the user has no todos, the export still includes the user’s account identifiers with an empty todos collection. Implementations SHOULD apply rate limiting/cooldowns to prevent abuse. Overdue/due-today indicators—if included by the export schema—are computed at generation time based on due_date using a consistent timezone policy (default: Asia/Seoul when the user has not selected a timezone).
operations.summary: Create a personal data export composed from todo_users and todo_todos (read-only)

requestBody.description: Optional parameters controlling export options for the authenticated user.

responseBody.description: Export job metadata for the user-scoped personal data export, including the exportId used to retrieve it later.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: Retrieve a previously created Personal Data Export identified by exportId (UUID). The export content is computed from todo_users and todo_todos for the authenticated requester and persisted as an export resource. This operation reads the export metadata and, depending on policy, may include a signed URI for downloading the generated artifact. Sensitive authentication material (e.g., password_hash) and session internals are never included in export content.
operations.description:
Return the personal data export created for the authenticated user. The export aggregates user account identifiers from todo_users (id, email, created_at, updated_at) and owned todos from todo_todos (id, title, description, due_date, completed, created_at, updated_at) filtered by ownership through todo_user_id. The models’ schema comments emphasize strict one-user ownership for todos and deterministic timestamps for ordering and audit expectations. Sensitive authentication material such as password_hash and session internals are explicitly excluded from export content and retrieval payloads.

Access control ensures only the user who initiated the export can retrieve it. Unauthenticated requests are denied, and users cannot access export results belonging to other principals. The retrieval is read-only with respect to domain tables and returns export metadata and, if applicable, a download URI for the generated artifact (e.g., JSON). Items hard-deleted prior to export creation are not present because todo_todos uses permanent deletion in MVP. If the artifact has expired, clients should re-create an export via POST /todo/user/reports/personalData.

Error handling includes: not found (unknown or expired exportId), permission denial (export not owned by requester), and artifact expiry requiring regeneration. Due/overdue indicators—if present in the artifact—are computed by application logic using date-only semantics and a consistent timezone policy (default Asia/Seoul when user-specific timezone is not configured).

operations.specification:
Delete a user account from the todo_users table. This operation permanently removes the authenticated user’s account identified by the path parameter userId (UUID) from the Prisma model todo_users. According to the schema, todo_users holds the unique login identifier (email), password_hash, and creation/update timestamps. Due to explicit foreign-key relations defined with onDelete: Cascade in related models, removing a row from todo_users will also remove dependent rows in:

- todo_user_sessions (authentication sessions belonging to the user)
- todo_todos (all personal todos owned by the user)
- todo_audit_events records that reference this user via todo_user_id

The business intent aligns with the requirements stating account deletion in MVP is permanent. The provider must enforce that a user can delete only their own account, and that the userId is a valid UUID corresponding to the authenticated principal. No request body is required, and the operation returns no response body.
operations.description:
Remove the authenticated user’s account identified by userId. The Prisma model todo_users represents authenticating user accounts for the minimal todo service, including a unique email, a password_hash, and created_at/updated_at timestamps used for ordering and audit expectations. The model’s documentation clarifies that account deletion in the MVP is permanent. Once the account is removed, it cannot be recovered and login using prior credentials is no longer possible.

Security and authorization: Only the authenticated owner should be allowed to delete their own account. Implementations must verify that the principal matches the path parameter userId. Requests from an unauthenticated state or attempts to delete an account other than the requester’s must be denied. After successful deletion, all active sessions for this user are invalidated as a result of cascading deletions.

Relationships and cascading effects: The schema defines foreign key relations from todo_user_sessions and todo_todos back to todo_users with onDelete: Cascade, ensuring that deleting a user also removes the user’s sessions and all owned todos. The todo_audit_events table can also reference todo_users by todo_user_id and uses the same cascading behavior; records that reference the deleted user will be removed accordingly. These cascades preserve referential integrity and prevent orphaned rows.

Validation and expected behavior: The userId path parameter is a UUID string that must correspond to an existing user. If the user does not exist, the provider should respond that the resource is not available. The operation requires no request body and returns no response body. Providers should ensure idempotent semantics from the client perspective: repeating a delete on an already removed account should consistently indicate that the resource is not available. Rate limiting and additional safety checks (e.g., recent authentication) may be applied at the business layer.

Related operations: Account lifecycle flows include registration, authentication (login), and logout, which create and manage todo_user_sessions and allow the user to perform protected actions. After deletion, all associated sessions are removed and future logins using the same credentials are prevented, consistent with the lifecycle expectations described in the requirements.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

email.description: Unique login identifier in email format to be persisted in Actors.todo_users.email. Must be unique per @@unique([email]) in Prisma schema.

password.description: Plaintext password supplied by the registrant. Backend hashes this value and stores it in todo_users.password_hash. Business rules: at least 8 characters, includes at least one letter and one number. Do NOT send pre-hashed values.

ip.description: Client IP address for session context captured in Actors.todo_user_sessions.ip. Optional; server can infer when omitted or null. When provided, must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation.

href.description: Connection URL at the time of registration. Stored as todo_user_sessions.href for the initial session record. DB column is VarChar(80000); constraint reflected here for consistency.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at the time of registration. Stored as todo_user_sessions.referrer for the initial session record. May be an empty string to indicate direct navigation without a referrer. DB column is VarChar(80000); constraint reflected here for consistency.

Security: never includes password_hash and never accepts server-managed fields (ids, timestamps). Session context fields (href, referrer required; ip optional) are included per authentication operation rules. This DTO is a composite request and does not directly map to a single Prisma model.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user (todo_users.id).

email.description: Unique login identifier for the user in email format. Maps to todo_users.email. Business rule: unique per user.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Maps to todo_users.created_at.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated. Maps to todo_users.updated_at.

user.description: Optional summary view of the authenticated user for immediate client initialization. Excludes sensitive credentials.

ITodoUser.IAuthorized.description: Authentication success response for user flows (login and refresh). Provides the authenticated user's id and the issued authorization token, and may include a lightweight user summary for client bootstrap.

id.description: Primary key of the user. Maps to todo_users.id (UUID).

email.description: Unique login identifier for the user (email). Mirrors todo_users.email. Exposed for identification in administrative and reference contexts; never includes password data.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated. Mirrors todo_users.updated_at.

ITodoUser.ISummary.description: User summary DTO for Actors.todo_users used exclusively as a reference object in other DTOs (e.g., audit events, sessions, todos). This summary deliberately excludes sensitive authentication data such as password_hash while preserving minimal identifying attributes and timestamps for context.

email.description: User's unique email identifier used for authentication. Maps to todo_users.email in Prisma schema; uniqueness enforced at database level.

password.description: Plain text password provided by the user for verification. The backend hashes this value and compares it with todo_users.password_hash. Must be at least 8 characters and include at least one letter and one number. Clients MUST NOT send pre-hashed passwords.

ip.description: Client IP address for session context when establishing login, used to populate todo_user_sessions.ip. Optional and may be omitted if the server derives it. When present, should be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation.

href.description: Request URL at the time of login, captured for session context (todo_user_sessions.href). Database column is VarChar(80000); this DTO mirrors that limit for consistency and validation.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at the time of login, captured for session context (todo_user_sessions.referrer). Database column is VarChar(80000); this DTO mirrors that limit. Allow empty string to represent direct navigation with no referrer; otherwise a valid URI string is required.

ITodoUser.ILogin.description: Login request DTO for authenticating against todo_users and establishing a session in todo_user_sessions. Includes session context fields (href, referrer required; ip optional) per security and audit requirements. This schema intentionally does not include any identity IDs as they are determined by authentication, and it does not map to a Prisma model (no x-autobe-prisma-schema).

refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token (or equivalent renewal proof) presented to obtain new access credentials. Storage and transport are implementation-specific; commonly held in an HTTP-only cookie, but included here as request body when applicable.

ITodoUser.IRefresh.description: Refresh request DTO to renew access credentials for an already authenticated user context. Does not include session context fields because refresh reuses existing session state by policy. This type does not map directly to a Prisma model.

id.description: Primary key of the user. Maps to todo_users.id (UUID).

email.description: Unique login identifier for the user in email format. Maps to todo_users.email. Business rule: unique per user.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated. Maps to todo_users.updated_at.

ITodoUser.description: User entity representing an authenticating account in the minimal todo service. Derived from Prisma model todo_users. Sensitive credential fields such as password_hash are intentionally excluded from response DTOs for security. The model owns personal todos (todo_todos) but reverse collections are not included to avoid actor reverse aggregations.

current_password.description: The user's current password in plaintext for verification. The server hashes and compares against todo_users.password_hash. Must be at least 8 characters and include at least one letter and one number to match policy; plaintext is accepted only transiently and is never persisted.

new_password.description: The new password in plaintext to be hashed and persisted to todo_users.password_hash. Must be at least 8 characters and include at least one letter and one number. Plaintext is accepted only transiently and is never persisted.

ITodoUser.IUpdatePassword.description: Request body schema for rotating the authenticated user's password. Affects Prisma model todo_users by updating password_hash and updated_at. Do not include any identity fields (e.g., user id) as they are derived from the authenticated context; session metadata (ip, href, referrer) is captured server-side for audit events.

id.description: Primary key of the todo item (todo_todos.id).

title.description: Required single-line short text naming the task from Prisma model todo_todos.title. Business rules per schema comments: 1–120 characters after trimming; no line breaks or control characters.

description.description: Optional multi-line details elaborating the task (todo_todos.description). When absent, use null. Business rule: up to 1,000 characters after trimming; store as absent when empty.

due_date.description: Optional date-only due date in ISO 8601 calendar date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Although stored as a timestamp at the database level (todo_todos.due_date), application logic interprets and exposes it as a date-only concept. Null when not set.

completed.description: Completion status (todo_todos.completed). false = not completed; true = completed.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (todo_todos.created_at). Used for default ordering and audit expectations.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (todo_todos.updated_at). Used as deterministic secondary ordering key.

user.description: Owning user transformed from foreign key todo_todos.todo_user_id referencing todo_users.id. Provided as ITodoUser.ISummary under the property name 'user' for cross-variant consistency.

ITodoTodo.description: Todo entity mapped to Prisma model todo_todos. Sensitive ownership FK (todo_user_id) is not exposed directly; instead, the owner relation is provided as ITodoUser.ISummary under the property name 'user' for cross-variant consistency. Overdue/due-today are computed at runtime and not stored.

ITodoTodo.ICreate.description: Create DTO for personal todo items. Corresponds to the Prisma model todo_todos. Ownership (todo_user_id), completion default (completed=false), and system timestamps (created_at/updated_at) are managed by the server and must not be provided by clients. Path parameters (e.g., todoId) must not be duplicated in the body.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion/redaction timestamp for the audit row. Null means active. Mirrors nullable todo_audit_events.deleted_at.

user.description: Reference to the acting user transformed from todo_audit_events.todo_user_id. Uses summary view to avoid circular expansion.

userSession.description: Reference to the originating session transformed from todo_audit_events.todo_user_session_id. Uses summary view to avoid circular expansion.

todo.description: Reference to the affected todo transformed from todo_audit_events.todo_todo_id. Uses summary view to avoid circular expansion.

ITodoAuditEvent.description: Audit trail entity from Prisma model todo_audit_events. Captures security- and business-relevant events such as registration, login/logout, todo CRUD, and unauthorized attempts. Foreign keys (todo_user_id, todo_user_session_id, todo_todo_id) are transformed to reference objects (Summary variants) to provide context while preventing circular references. Sensitive authentication material is never included. href/referrer include DB-aligned max length for completeness.

id.description: Primary key of the session. Maps to todo_user_sessions.id (UUID).

ip.description: Client IP address recorded at session establishment. Mirrors todo_user_sessions.ip. Textual IPv4/IPv6 representation as captured by the server.

href.description: Request URL at session establishment. Mirrors todo_user_sessions.href (VarChar(80000)). Always present and a valid URI.

referrer.description: Referrer URL at session establishment. Mirrors todo_user_sessions.referrer (VarChar(80000)). Business semantics allow an empty string to represent direct navigation with no referrer; otherwise, a valid URI string is provided.

expired_at.description: Session end/invalidated time. Null means active or not yet recorded. Mirrors todo_user_sessions.expired_at.

user.description: Owning user of this session. Transforms todo_user_sessions.todo_user_id into a summary object to provide actor context without reverse collections.

ITodoUserSession.ISummary.description: User session summary DTO for Actors.todo_user_sessions. Includes connection context (ip, href, referrer), lifecycle timestamps (created_at, expired_at), and the owning user as a summary reference. This type omits any token materials by design and is safe for documentation and list views. href/referrer align with Prisma VarChar(80000); referrer allows empty string to denote direct navigation.

id.description: Primary key of the todo. Maps to todo_todos.id (UUID).

title.description: Required single-line short text naming the task (1–120 characters after trimming; no line breaks). Mirrors todo_todos.title.

due_date.description: Optional date-only due date as stored in the database (timestamp). Application logic interprets and presents this value as a date-only concept. Mirrors todo_todos.due_date.

completed.description: Completion status of the task. false for not completed, true for completed. Mirrors todo_todos.completed.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp of the todo. Mirrors todo_todos.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp of the todo. Mirrors todo_todos.updated_at.

owner.description: Owning user transformed from foreign key todo_todos.todo_user_id referencing todo_users.id. Provided as ITodoUser.ISummary under the property name 'owner' for cross-variant consistency.

ITodoTodo.ISummary.description: Todo summary DTO for Todos.todo_todos designed for list and embedding contexts. Provides core fields (id, title, completed, timestamps) and lightweight context (owner user) while omitting heavy collections. The due date is represented as a nullable timestamp but interpreted as date-only at the application level.

include_overdue_flags.description: When true, the export includes computed boolean flags per todo (overdue, due_today) evaluated at generation time using the product’s timezone policy (default Asia/Seoul when user has not selected a timezone).

ITodoUserPersonalDataExport.ICreate.description: Request body for creating a user-scoped personal data export. This is a computed, read-only aggregation over todo_users and todo_todos; it does not map to a single Prisma model. No actor identifiers are accepted—identity is taken from the authenticated session. Optional flags control inclusion of computed fields in the export payload.

id.description: Unique identifier of the personal data export job (exportId). This identifier is used to retrieve the export later. The export resource is a computed artifact and does not map to a single Prisma model.

status.description: Current lifecycle status of the personal data export job. Implementations typically progress from pending/processing to ready; expired and failed reflect retention/processing outcomes.

requested_at.description: Timestamp when the export job was created. This reflects the moment the system accepted the request and began composing content.

expires_at.description: Optional expiration timestamp after which the generated artifact is no longer retrievable. Null indicates the artifact does not expire or an expiration policy is not applied.

download_uri.description: Optional signed URI to download the generated artifact (e.g., JSON file). Present only when the job is ready and a downloadable artifact is available.

user.description: Snapshot of the authenticated user’s account identifiers composed from the todo_users model. Sensitive authentication fields (e.g., password_hash) are EXCLUDED from this snapshot.

todos.description: Array of the owner’s todos composed from the todo_todos model. Includes the business-visible fields required by export (id, title, description, due_date, completed, created_at, updated_at). May be empty when the user has no todos.

todos_count.description: Total number of todos included in this export for convenience. Should equal the length of the todos array.

ITodoUserPersonalDataExport.description: Personal Data Export resource composed from multiple domain models for the authenticated user. The content is read-only with respect to domain tables and may be generated asynchronously. The export aggregates: (1) the user’s account identifiers from Prisma model todo_users (id, email, created_at, updated_at) while explicitly excluding sensitive authentication material like password_hash; and (2) the user’s owned todos from Prisma model todo_todos (id, title, description, due_date, completed, created_at, updated_at) filtered by ownership via todo_user_id. An audit event may be recorded in todo_audit_events as an internal side effect but is not exposed in this response. This schema does not map to a single Prisma model and represents a composed artifact.

updated_at.description: Last account update timestamp from todo_users.updated_at.

ITodoUserExportSnapshot.description: A minimal snapshot of a user account composed directly from Prisma model todo_users. Only public identifiers are included (id, email, created_at, updated_at). The sensitive password_hash column is intentionally excluded from all response DTOs.

title.description: Required single-line title from todo_todos.title. Must be 1–120 characters after trimming and contain no line breaks.

description.description: Optional details from todo_todos.description. Provide up to 1,000 characters after trimming or null to indicate absence.

due_date.description: Optional date-only due date derived from todo_todos.due_date. Although stored as a timestamp type, it is interpreted as a calendar date without time-of-day in business semantics. Null indicates no due date.

completed.description: Completion state from todo_todos.completed (false = not completed, true = completed).

created_at.description: Creation timestamp from todo_todos.created_at used for default ordering.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp from todo_todos.updated_at used for deterministic secondary ordering.

ITodoTodoExportSnapshot.description: A snapshot of a todo item composed directly from Prisma model todo_todos for export purposes. Fields reflect the business-visible columns only; ownership is enforced by todo_user_id at query time and is not included in this snapshot.

id.description: Primary key of the audit event record. Maps to todo_audit_events.id (UUID).

actor_type.description: Actor class that originated the event (e.g., "user", "system"). Mirrors todo_audit_events.actor_type. Used for high-level filtering without joins.

category.description: High-level category for the event such as "auth", "todo", or "security". Matches todo_audit_events.category.

action.description: Concrete action keyword, for example: "register", "login", "logout", "todo_create", "todo_update", "todo_delete", or "unauthorized_attempt". Mirrors todo_audit_events.action.

success.description: Whether the attempted action succeeded (true) or failed (false). Maps to todo_audit_events.success.

message.description: Optional human-readable summary intended for operator review. Mirrors nullable todo_audit_events.message.

ip.description: Client IP address captured when the event was recorded. When present, must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation. Mirrors nullable todo_audit_events.ip.

href.description: Request URL at the time of the event. Mirrors nullable todo_audit_events.href (VarChar(80000)).

referrer.description: Referrer URL associated with the request at the time of the event. Mirrors nullable todo_audit_events.referrer (VarChar(80000)).

resource_type.description: Type name of the affected resource (e.g., "user", "todo"). Present when the event pertains to a specific resource. Mirrors nullable todo_audit_events.resource_type.

resource_id.description: Opaque identifier of the affected resource when the event refers to a specific entity. Mirrors nullable todo_audit_events.resource_id (UUID). Not a foreign key to allow polymorphism.

created_at.description: Event creation timestamp (when the event was recorded). Mirrors todo_audit_events.created_at.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this audit row. Mirrors todo_audit_events.updated_at.

user.description: Authenticated user who performed the action, when available. Transforms todo_audit_events.todo_user_id (nullable FK) into an object reference. Uses ITodoUser.ISummary to prevent circular expansion.

userSession.description: Originating session for the action, when available. Transforms todo_audit_events.todo_user_session_id (nullable FK) into an object reference. Uses ITodoUserSession.ISummary to avoid deep expansion.

todo.description: Target todo resource when the event pertains to a specific todo item. Transforms todo_audit_events.todo_todo_id (nullable FK) into an object reference. Uses ITodoTodo.ISummary.

ITodoAuditEvent.ISummary.description:
Audit event summary DTO representing a lightweight, list-optimized view of Systematic.todo_audit_events. This type exposes essential categorization, outcome, context, and timestamps while transforming nullable foreign keys (todo_user_id, todo_user_session_id, todo_todo_id) into optional summary references to prevent circular expansion.

Source: Prisma model todo_audit_events. Fields map directly to columns documented in the Prisma schema (actor_type, category, action, success, message, ip, href, referrer, resource_type, resource_id, created_at, updated_at). Soft deletion (deleted_at) exists in the table but is intentionally omitted from the summary view.
